hypotheses.justification: The statement elaborates without it: `Representation.character` is defined as `LinearMap.trace k V (ρ g)` and needs no finite-dimensionality (Mathlib `RepresentationTheory/Character.lean`; infinite-dimensional spaces just get a junk trace value). The proof never uses it either. It builds `IsIrreducible ρ` from `hirr` and `Nontrivial V`, gets `Invertible (Nat.card (GL2 q) : K)` from `CharZero`, then applies `Representation.char_orthonormal ρ ρ`. That lemma only assumes `[Fintype G] [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsIrreducible ρ] [IsIrreducible σ]`; it derives finite-dimensionality internally via `ρ.asModuleEquiv.finiteDimensional`. On paper it also follows from the other hypotheses: for any nonzero v (V is nontrivial), the span of the finite orbit G·v is a nonzero subrepresentation, so by `hirr` it is all of V, hence V is finite-dimensional. So the theorem holds and the same proof goes through without this binder.
